answer: An agent marketplace treats each trading identity as a graph vertex and requires a fixed bond, locked for 90 days, before granting it one order slot per minute. At the market’s inlet, even agents serving a digital wharf must post that bond; new names get no free capacity. An attacker seeking 1,000 times the throughput must lock 1,000 bonds, sacrificing liquidity and interest rather than gaining leverage merely by minting identities.
